priority_order: Remote jobs open to applicants based in Pakistan and international remote opportunities
Direct employer career pages and ATS listings
Small and newly established employers with suitable roles

salary_priority.rule: Aim for PKR 100,000/month or above. For urgent suitable opportunities, consider offers from PKR 60,000-70,000 upward; prefer at least PKR 70,000, and never state an expectation below PKR 60,000. If a salary range is published, negotiate toward its upper end or modestly above it when realistic, but remain flexible to avoid losing a suitable urgent opportunity. If no salary is published, state PKR 100,000/month. International salary: use employer's published local-currency range; otherwise Negotiable for text fields and manual review for mandatory numeric fields.

company_size_policy: Do not reject small, local, startup, newly established, or lesser-known employers merely because of company size. Also actively target established national companies and international multinationals.
urgent_job_policy: Keep matching broad enough to surface legitimate Graphic Designer and business/computer roles from small employers, local companies, established national companies, multinational companies, social-media job advertisements, and direct employer postings.
auto_apply_policy: Automatically submit public employer application forms when every required answer is supported by verified profile data or explicit application_preferences. Use matched CV. Answer international Pakistan citizenship and legal authorization: answer Yes for Pakistan work authorization. For other countries answer No to current work authorization and Yes to sponsorship required; relocation willing after legal procedures, estimated 1-2 months; one-week notice; willing to travel; willing to work shifts abroad. Pakistan salary target is PKR 100,000/month; for urgent suitable roles accept consideration from PKR 60,000-70,000 upward, prefer PKR 70,000 minimum, and never state an expectation below PKR 60,000. If a range is published, negotiate realistically toward its upper end. International salary uses published local salary range; never invent a numeric expectation when no range is available. Full-time and remote are priorities; internships, contract and temporary roles are acceptable when they offer a credible path to permanent full-time employment. Do not disclose hearing loss by default; mandatory medical/disability/accommodation questions require manual review. Never fabricate personal/legal answers or bypass CAPTCHA, 2FA, login walls, paid memberships, anti-bot controls, or platform restrictions. Unknown required questions stay for manual review. Daily limits: 30 Pakistan and 30 international.

search_strategy.google_discovery: Use Google-indexed web results to discover current vacancies on employer-owned career pages and direct application pages, not only job boards.
search_strategy.company_websites: Search national Pakistani companies, multinational companies, international employers, and their ATS/career domains directly through Google-indexed results.
search_strategy.direct_application: Prefer the employer's own application URL when a vacancy is found on a company career site; otherwise use the source's application method.
search_strategy.google_jobs: Include Google Jobs/Search discovery alongside Indeed, Rozee.pk, Glassdoor, Pakistani job boards, social posts, and direct employer career pages.
search_strategy.remote_jobs: Actively search remote and work-from-home roles in Pakistan and internationally; verify location eligibility because remote does not always mean worldwide.
search_strategy.flexjobs: Discover publicly indexed FlexJobs listings; if a listing requires FlexJobs membership, login, or a protected application flow, save it for manual review rather than bypassing access controls.

employment_type_policy: Prioritize permanent full-time and eligible remote roles. Also pursue internships, contract and temporary positions when the listing indicates a credible route or possibility of conversion to permanent full-time employment.
